hero.title:
Smaller. Faster.
Easier to use.
hero.description: A native Rust coding agent for reading and editing code, running commands and managing sessions in your terminal. Download one binary, configure a model and start coding. Extend it with plugins or embed the Rust SDK when you need more.

features.title: Smaller. One binary is enough.
features.description: A native binary with no extra Node.js runtime. Keep your terminal coding tool in one file, with less disk space and fewer dependencies.

features.title: Faster. Less startup waiting.
features.description: Native Rust keeps startup and memory overhead low. Reproducible offline benchmarks cover cold start and memory at ready.

features.title: Easier. Open a terminal and go.
features.description: Prebuilt binaries need no Rust toolchain. Configure a model to edit files and run commands. Local sessions let you pick up interrupted work.

features.title: Need more? Make it your own.
features.description: Swap model providers, install Rust plugins or embed the core crates in your app. The same agent can be the foundation for your own tools.

releases.description: Edit, read and write panels share themed insets and status backgrounds. Changelog version parsing is fixed, and Linux and Windows PR checks now reject compiler warnings.

releases.description: More provider adapters and a complete extension resource protocol.

releases.title: Your ideas
releases.description: Bring rpi into your product, your workflow and your own runtime.

packages.rpi-cli: Terminal coding-agent CLI with the rpi command, interactive TUI, configuration and plugin loading.
packages.rpi-agent: Async Agent runtime and loop with AgentTool, events, hooks and message queues.
packages.rpi-tools: Pi-compatible read, write, edit and bash tools with ExecutionEnv.
packages.rpi-plugin-sdk: Stable #[repr(C)] ABI contract for Rust cdylib plugins; plugins depend only on this boundary.
packages.rpi-extensions: Host-side dynamic plugin loader that adapts ABI plugins into AgentTool and manages lifecycle.
packages.rpi-harness: Session trees, JSONL persistence, context compaction and the AgentHarness run loop.
packages.rpi-mcp-adapter: MCP tools over persistent stdio and Streamable HTTP connections. Discover and call tools with mcp_list and mcp_call.
packages.rpi-web-access: Constrained public web fetching with redirect, credential, private-address and response-size limits.
packages.rpi-subagents: Build bounded delegation requests with role, turn and timeout limits for host scheduling.
packages.rpi-background-tasks: Trackable background process extension with start, status, list and cancel operations.
packages.rpi-lens: Bounded local code diagnostics extension with allowlisted checks, timeout and output limits.
packages.rpi-todo: Session task lists with pending, in-progress and completed states, restored from the active branch and displayed in the terminal.
packages.rpi-codegraph: Bounded local source-file and import graph tool for multiple languages.
packages.rpi-memory: Local persistent memory tool with remember, recall, list, forget and clear actions.
packages.rpi-token-usage: Deterministic token estimate tool and compact usage message renderer for TUI hosts.
packages.rpi-ask-user: Structured question tool compatible with Pi's native shape, including single-select, multi-select and custom input.
packages.rpi-permissions: Native-compatible persistent permission policy with Tool(pattern) rules and check, grant, revoke and list actions.
packages.rpi-simplify: Read-only local code review tool for long lines, TODOs, adjacent duplicates and function counts.
packages.rpi-search: Bounded local filename and content search that skips dependency and build directories.
packages.rpi-goal: Persistent project goals with /goal, pause and resume, turn and time budgets, and goal context injected into the conversation.
packages.rpi-websearch: Keyless web reference search combining DuckDuckGo and Wikipedia with bounded titles, URLs, snippets and sources.
packages.rpi-webfetch: Bounded public HTTP(S) page reader that blocks private DNS targets and returns fetch failures as tool results.
packages.rpi-firecrawl: Firecrawl-backed web search and scrape tools for the rpi Agent.
packages.rpi-extension-rpc: Cross-platform JSONL extension RPC client and localhost server with bounded requests and timeouts.
packages.rpi-im-message: Persistent Feishu/Lark messaging over a long connection, with multiple profiles and a headless message service.
packages.rpi-server: TCP JSONL server for rpi with streaming subscriptions and Transport trait abstraction, launchable via rpi --server.
packages.rpi-acp: Use rpi in Zed and other ACP clients, with streamed replies, persistent sessions, restore and cancellation.
packages.rpi-run-stats: Live terminal monitoring for turns, steps, TPS, TTFT, TPM, errors and cost. Toggle with /stats or F8.
packages.rpi-plan-mode: Session planning mode with read-only exploration, /plan commands, restored branch plans and progress display.
packages.rpi-langfuse: Langfuse observability for model, tool and session events, plus scoring and prompt-management tools.
packages.rpi-voice: Terminal voice conversations with push-to-talk, offline speech recognition, spoken replies and a pet panel.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.intro: Guides and SDK references to take you from your first faux Agent to tools, sessions and plugins.

guide.label: User guide
guide.description: For developers new to rpi: install it, run it and connect an Agent to your own application.

complete-guide.title: Complete user guide
complete-guide.summary: The full path from install, model config, .rpi resources and Rust plugins to SDK integration, troubleshooting and release.
body: The website docs stay in sync with /user-guide.md in the repository. A fresh rpi install ships the core tools by default and adds more through Rust cdylib extensions built with rpi-plugin-sdk.
Start with install and first run, then move on to Provider setup, Rust extensions, Agent project structure or SDK integration as needed.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.summary: Run the full loop with the faux provider first; no API key or network is required.
body: rpi is a library-first Rust Agent toolkit. Run the repository's minimal example, then compose rpi-ai, rpi-agent and rpi-tools as needed.
The faux provider returns deterministic local responses, making it useful for learning event streams, writing tests and validating the tool loop.
links: README / How you build an agent

install.title: Install and run
install.summary: Rust 1.78+, Cargo and Tokio are the minimum; you can also install rpi-cli directly.
body: Run cargo install rpi-cli when you only need the CLI. Clone the repository and run the minimal example when you want to study the Agent loop. Cargo builds the workspace in dependency order.
Provide real Provider credentials through CLI flags, ~/.rpi/auth.json, models.json or environment variables. Never commit secrets.

code.content:
# Install the CLI
cargo install rpi-cli
rpi -p "hello"

# Run the example from source
git clone https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust.git
cd pi-rust
cargo run -p minimal

first-agent.title: Your first Agent
first-agent.summary: Declare a model, system prompt and tools with AgentBuilder, then subscribe to events and send a prompt.
body: AgentBuilder gathers runtime dependencies during construction; Agent owns messages, events and pending prompts. Subscribe before calling prompt.
Production applications usually map events to UI or telemetry. Tests can collect AgentEnd events for assertions.

tools.title: Add tools
tools.summary: Add AgentTool to the builder; Pi-compatible tools isolate filesystem and command execution through ExecutionEnv.
body: rpi-tools provides the Pi-compatible read, write, edit and bash tools. Writes are serialized through MutationQueue.
Use InMemoryExecutionEnv in tests to avoid the real filesystem. Implement rpi-agent's AgentTool trait for custom tools.

providers.title: Configure a Provider
providers.summary: The shared Model / Provider abstraction makes Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible and faux providers interchangeable.
body: The default model is selected from authenticated models. Put a custom gateway in ~/.rpi/agent/models.json and select it as provider/model in the CLI.
Anthropic supports ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN. OpenAI-compatible endpoints use the openai-completions API setting.

sessions.title: Sessions and Harness
sessions.summary: Hand the Agent to AgentHarness when you need persistence, compaction and context files.
body: rpi-harness combines session trees, JSONL persistence, compaction, skills, prompt templates and context files above Agent. The core Agent stays independently usable.
Treat the session id as a stable product identifier and use the JSONL backend for replayable events and messages.

extensions.title: Plugins and extensions
extensions.summary: Use stable-ABI cdylib plugins to register tools, Providers, commands and resources.
body: Plugin crates depend on rpi-plugin-sdk and export rpi_plugin_register to receive PluginApiVt. rpi-extensions discovers, loads, registers and manages their lifecycle.
Keep cross-boundary data inside SDK serializable types; plugins should not depend on private host modules.

testing.title: Testing with the faux provider
testing.summary: Make models and execution environments replaceable so tests target Agent behavior rather than the network.
body: The faux provider verifies message order, tool calls and AgentEnd. InMemoryExecutionEnv verifies file tools. Together they make fully offline integration tests possible.
Add a small set of HTTP fixture tests around Provider adapters for streaming parsing, error mapping and tool argument validation.

sdk.label: SDK reference
sdk.description: Find API boundaries by crate and core trait when implementing a custom Provider, tool, Harness or plugin.

crate-overview.title: Crate overview
crate-overview.summary: The workspace keeps one-way dependencies from telemetry and AI types up to the CLI.
body: Published names use the rpi- prefix while disk directories retain their pi-* history. Core crates can be embedded without the CLI.
The typical dependency direction is rpi-telemetry -> rpi-ai -> rpi-agent -> rpi-tools -> rpi-harness -> rpi-cli.

rpi-ai.title: rpi-ai
rpi-ai.summary: Unified Model, Provider, Message, Context and streaming AssistantMessageEvent types.
body: Provider converts a shared request into a model API call and maps the response back into SDK events. validate_tool_arguments checks JSON before execution.
When implementing a Provider, reuse shared message and streaming event types instead of leaking vendor-specific structures upward.

rpi-agent.title: rpi-agent
rpi-agent.summary: Agent, AgentBuilder, AgentTool, AgentEvent and run_agent_loop form the runtime core.
body: AgentBuilder assembles the model, system prompt, tools and hooks. run_agent_loop advances messages, tool calls and Provider streams.
PendingMessageQueue accepts new user messages while a run is active; AgentEvent subscriptions can drive UI and telemetry.

rpi-tools.title: rpi-tools
rpi-tools.summary: ExecutionEnv isolates filesystem, process and path operations used by tools.
body: OsExecutionEnv connects to the operating system; InMemoryExecutionEnv provides an in-memory implementation for tests. create_*_tool returns registerable AgentTools.
Serialize high-risk writes through MutationQueue and add confirmation policy at the product layer.

rpi-harness.title: rpi-harness
rpi-harness.summary: Sessions, compaction, skills, templates and context files built above Agent.
body: Harness is the product integration layer: it restores sessions, trims context, loads skills and builds the Context for a run.
Use rpi-agent directly for one-off calls and add Harness when persistence is needed.

lifecycle.title: Agent lifecycle
lifecycle.summary: Build, subscribe, prompt, tool loop and end event are the minimum lifecycle.
body: Subscribe after creating an Agent and before sending a prompt. Provider deltas and tool calls return to the loop, which ends with AgentEnd.
Use hooks for logging, policy and UI synchronization without changing the core message contract.

events.title: Provider and AgentEvent
events.summary: A shared event stream connects models, runtime and frontend without leaking vendor protocols into the UI.
body: AssistantMessageEventStream expresses text deltas, tool calls and stop reasons. AgentEvent adds tool execution and run lifecycle events.
Render UI incrementally from events; persist the complete message and usage at the end.

plugin-abi.title: Plugin ABI
plugin-abi.summary: rpi-plugin-sdk is the only boundary plugins and hosts should depend on.
body: Plugins compile as cdylib and are discovered by rpi-extensions. The registry stores tools, Providers, events and resource handlers while the host owns unloading and isolation.
Bump the ABI version for breaking changes and update plugin-stub plus smoke tests together. Do not link plugins to private rpi-cli modules.
